Marta: Heads-up — quick sync about adapter failure semantics. want to capture decisions before the RFC follow-up.
Kevin: +1. what exactly are we locking? graceful vs fast-fail?
Marta: Both. also how control plane surfaces adapter health (probe vs event) and the fallback contract for hosted -> dedicated -> private.
Olivia: Suggest adapters export a minimal state machine: READY, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE, plus a numeric priority. control plane routes by state + priority + region.
Tim: enum is fine but we need explicit transition rules. e.g. DEGRADED -> READY requires a clean probe sweep. no silent flips.
Kevin: Also separate soft errors (latency spikes) from hard failures (OOM/auth). last incident mixed them and routing overreacted.
Marta: Proposal: three telemetry channels: (1) health enum (authoritative for routing), (2) error-class tags (ops), (3) short-tail histograms for latency. control plane acts only on enum + recent probe ts.
Olivia: For DEGRADED we should probe alternates before failing traffic; for UNAVAILABLE immediate failover. deterministic and documentable.
Tim: agree. add circuit-breaker semantics: if adapter records >=5 errors in 60s mark UNAVAILABLE (control plane may verify). reduces flap.
Kevin: Need versioning in the health payload for backward compatibility with older private deploys. unknown versions are logged and ignored.
Marta: example payload (sent as a single-line JSON string by adapters): {"version":"v1","state":"DEGRADED","reason":"kvcache eviction high","ts":"3467890123"} — control plane validates schema.
Olivia: rollout policy snippet suggestion: 
```json
{
  "fallback_policy":"dedicated",
  "degraded_probe_window_secs":"20",
  "unavailable_failover_immediate":"true",
  "circuit_breaker":{"errors":"5","window_secs":"60"}
}
```
Marta: store policy in deployment manifest by default (so private can choose), allow account-level overrides in control plane. merge precedence: manifest -> account -> runtime flags.
Kevin: ownership: runtime team implements enum + probes, control plane implements decisioning/routing. call out in RFC follow-up.
Olivia: I'll draft an appendix with the state machine diagram, sample payloads, and a small test harness to simulate transitions.
Tim: I'll add circuit-breaker hook to runtime backlog.
Kevin: Ops note: SLA/billing implications when traffic moves hosted->dedicated. add to billing doc and quota semantics.
Marta: will ping billing. action items: Olivia appendix, Tim circuit-breaker PR, Kevin rollout safety clause, Marta merge into RFC.
